skills.name: benchmarking

skills.name: build

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("number.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("number.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use crate::mem;
15. 
16. //==================================================================================================
17. // Structures
18. //==================================================================================================
19. 
20. ///
21. /// # Description
22. ///
23. /// A type that represents a frame number.
24. /// A frame number is in the range from `0` to [`Self::MAX`] (inclusive).
25. ///
26. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
27. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
28. pub struct FrameNumber(usize);
29. 
30. //==================================================================================================
31. // Implementations
32. //==================================================================================================
33. 
34. impl FrameNumber {
35.     /// The maximum frame number.
36.     #[verus_verify]
37.     pub const MAX: usize = mem::MAX_ADDRESS / mem::FRAME_SIZE - 1;
38. 
39.     pub const NULL: Self = Self(0);
40. 
41.     ///
42.     /// # Description
43.     ///
44.     /// Converts a [`FrameNumber`] into a raw value.
45.     ///
46.     /// # Returns
47.     ///
48.     /// The raw value of the target [`FrameNumber`].
49.     ///
50.     // Pure newtype-identity projection: the returned raw value equals the
51.     // abstract frame index (`result as int == self@`). The type invariant
52.     // additionally bounds it to `0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()`, which callers
53.     // (`pde.rs`/`pte.rs` `<< FRAME_SHIFT`, `phys.rs::from_number` `* FRAME_SIZE`,
54.     // `frame.rs` refcount indexing) rely on for their no-overflow proofs.
55.     #[verus_spec(result =>
56.         ensures
57.             result as int == self@,
58.             0 <= result as int <= spec_max_frame_number(),
59.     )]
60.     pub fn into_raw_value(self) -> usize {
61.         proof! { use_type_invariant(&self); }
62.         self.0
63.     }
64. }
65. 
66. #[verus_verify]
67. impl FrameNumber {
68.     ///
69.     /// # Description
70.     ///
71.     /// Constructs a [`FrameNumber`].
72.     ///
73.     /// # Parameters
74.     ///
75.     /// - `value`: The value of the frame number.
76.     ///
77.     /// # Returns
78.     ///
79.     /// - `Some(`[`FrameNumber`]`)`: Upon success.
80.     /// - `None`: If the value is greater than [`Self::MAX`].
81.     ///
82.     // Validating constructor. `Some` is returned **iff** `value` is a
83.     // representable frame index (`value <= spec_max_frame_number()`), which is
84.     // the only failure signal (`None` otherwise — bidirectional). On success the
85.     // index is preserved exactly (`f@ == value as int`) and the result is
86.     // well-formed (`f.inv()`). Together with `into_raw_value` this yields the
87.     // round-trip identity `from_raw_value(v).unwrap().into_raw_value() == v`.
88.     #[verus_spec(result =>
89.         ensures
90.             (result is Some) <==> (value as int <= spec_max_frame_number()),
91.             result matches Some(f) ==> f@ == value as int && f.inv(),
92.     )]
93.     pub fn from_raw_value(value: usize) -> Option<Self> {
94.         if value > Self::MAX {
95.             return None;
96.         }
97. 
98.         Some(Self(value))
99.     }
100. }
101. 
102. //==================================================================================================
103. // Unit Tests
104. //==================================================================================================
105. 
106. /// Tests if [`FrameNumber::from_raw_value()`] successfully constructs frame zero.
107. #[test]
108. fn test_frame_number_from_raw_value_zero() {
109.     let raw_value: usize = 0;
110.     let frame_number: FrameNumber = FrameNumber::from_raw_value(raw_value).unwrap();
111.     assert_eq!(frame_number.into_raw_value(), raw_value);
112. }
113. 
114. /// Tests if [`FrameNumber::from_raw_value()`] successfully constructs the maximum frame number.
115. #[test]
116. fn test_frame_number_from_raw_value_max() {
117.     let raw_value: usize = FrameNumber::MAX;
118.     let frame_number: FrameNumber = FrameNumber::from_raw_value(raw_value).unwrap();
119.     assert_eq!(frame_number.into_raw_value(), raw_value);
120. }
121.

2. 
3. // ── Frame size / representability bound ───────────────────────────────────────
4. //
5. // `FrameNumber` is, to its callers, the abstract identity of one physical page
6. // frame: a bounded non-negative integer index. The two spec constants below fix
7. // the vocabulary every contract speaks. They share the names the upstream
8. // callers already trust in `phys.spec.rs` / `tcb-allowed.md`, so the in-module
9. // contracts and the callers' assumed contracts coincide by construction.
10. 
11. // The frame size as an unbounded integer, tied to the exec `mem::FRAME_SIZE`
12. // (an alias of `PAGE_SIZE`). Strictly positive; positivity is the load-bearing
13. // fact behind the no-overflow reasoning of every caller that scales a frame
14. // index by the frame size.
15. pub open spec fn spec_frame_size() -> int {
16.     mem::FRAME_SIZE as int
17. }
18. 
19. // The inclusive maximum frame index, mirroring the exec
20. // `FrameNumber::MAX == mem::MAX_ADDRESS / mem::FRAME_SIZE - 1`. A frame index in
21. // `0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()` scaled by `spec_frame_size()` stays within
22. // `usize`, which is exactly the no-overflow guarantee `phys.rs::from_number`,
23. // `pde.rs` and `pte.rs` depend on.
24. pub open spec fn spec_max_frame_number() -> int {
25.     mem::MAX_ADDRESS as int / spec_frame_size() - 1
26. }
27. 
28. // ── View ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
29. //
30. // A `FrameNumber` abstracts to a single mathematical integer: the raw frame
31. // index. `closed` so the `usize`-newtype mapping does not leak; callers still
32. // obtain a usable `int` (`f@`) for indexing, arithmetic and comparison, while
33. // the concrete `usize` is recovered through `into_raw_value`'s contract
34. // (`result as int == self@`).
35. impl View for FrameNumber {
36.     type V = int;
37. 
38.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
39.         self.0 as int
40.     }
41. }
42. 
43. // ── Well-formedness invariant ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
44. //
45. // Every `FrameNumber` names a representable frame: its index lies in
46. // `0 ..= spec_max_frame_number()`. Declared as a `#[verifier::type_invariant]`
47. // so the bound holds for *every* value of the type without a precondition —
48. // `into_raw_value`'s callers rely on the range unconditionally (they never hold
49. // a precondition obligation when projecting a frame they already own). Stated
50. // purely over the abstract index `self@`, independent of the inner `usize`.
51. impl FrameNumber {
52.     #[verifier::type_invariant]
53.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
54.         &&& 0 <= self@
55.         &&& self@ <= spec_max_frame_number()
56.     }
57. }
58. 
59. } // verus!
60.
